protocol.veribench_note: VeriBench functional semantic correctness scores from trustworthy-theorem-judges experiment 09 native-main CSVs, column final_score_0_5, integer grades 0 through 5. Clone commit 460466dd10b735c5ff25f9e9cb21f0441fcf960b. No artifact in that clone is named R_v1; this is the live experiment 09 numeric collection, not a frozen file called R_v1. Scored rows kept: 250. rater_id is the roster id stored with rater_name. Split group is item_id. The same person can rate items that land in different splits.

summary.name: summeval_expert_coherence
summary.notes: SummEval expert, aspect coherence only. SummEval expert annotations on four aspects (coherence, consistency, fluency, relevance), native grades 1–5 stored as class values [1,2,3,4,5]. Every summary has [3] expert annotation records. The jsonl does not publish a stable rater id, so rater_id is the within-item vote index, not a person. Split group is the source article (filepath), so every system and aspect of one article stays in one split. Binary views use the pre-registered cut grade ≥ 4.

summary.name: chaosNLI_snli
summary.notes: ChaosNLI SNLI or MNLI-matched, 3 classes, 100 votes per item in the author files. label_count order is entailment, neutral, contradiction. Ranked probability score uses that order as an imposed order (entailment < neutral < contradiction); it is not a native Likert scale. rater_id is a within-item vote index expanded from the counts, not a person. Each uid is its own split group.

summary.name: dices990
summary.notes: DICES-990 rater-level Q_overall. Yes means unsafe (DICES-990 README; DICES-350 uses the same question family). Order for ranked probability score: No < Unsure < Yes, values 0,1,2. Dropped 7217 rows whose rater_id is in the README quality-filter list (12 raters). rater_id is the released person id. Split group is item_id. Raters are crossed, so the same person can appear in train and test on different conversations; no conversation's raters are split.
